rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt: ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Homem do chapéu de ferro, the bronze-coloured colossal iron-hatted giant of Algarve legend. ANATOMY: one colossal bronze-coloured humanlike giant, one head, two eyes, two arms, two legs, an ENORMOUS broad iron hat sunk low onto head, a wide monstrous mouth; fully opaque dark coarse coat and trousers; one black pig companion at his foot, no horns or extra heads. MOMENT: Stride across the road toward the viewer and belch a strong physical tongue of orange fire from his gaping mouth, one huge hand reaching down toward tiny fleeing travellers below olive branches. POWER: Spits actual flames from mouth when enraged; flames illuminate bronze face and rusty iron brim, no generic body aura and no lightning attacks. SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle; subject fills frame, natural documented size, never unsupported gigantic. LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm lateral source, deep shadows, crisp rim, physically moving dust/water only. SURFACE: tactile coarse textures, rich walnut/antique-gold palette. SETTING: Algarve roadside at midnight, olive and fig trees and a spring; small human figures beside the giant's foot establish documented colossal size. MOOD: dangerous or awe-inspiring, never ordinary, cute, calm or decorative. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, symbols, logos, border, signature, watermark; no extra heads or limbs; no franchises; no nudity, transparent clothes, blood, wounds or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon lines or energy ribbons.
